questions.questionEn: An ambulance is stopped in a line of traffic at a red light while transporting a patient at routine (non-emergency) status. The patient's level of consciousness suddenly deteriorates and the attending paramedic asks the driver to upgrade to lights and sirens. What is the safest way for the driver to proceed?
questions.questionZh: 救护车正以普通（非紧急）状态转运患者，此刻停在红灯前的车流中。患者意识水平突然下降，随车救护员要求司机升级为灯笛模式。司机最安全的做法是什么？

options.en: Activate the lights and siren immediately so that the surrounding vehicles clear the way
options.zh: 立刻打开警灯和警笛，让周围车辆让路

options.en: Sound the horn repeatedly until the vehicle in front moves forward into the intersection
options.zh: 反复按喇叭，直到前车驶入路口

options.en: Wait until the light turns green and traffic begins to move, then activate the lights and siren
options.zh: 等到绿灯亮起、车流开始移动之后，再打开警灯和警笛

options.en: Pull onto the sidewalk and drive around the stopped line of traffic
options.zh: 把车开上人行道，绕过停着的车队

questions.explanationEn: Suddenly activating emergency lights and siren while boxed in at a red light startles drivers who have nowhere to go, and some will roll forward into the intersection against the red light and cause a collision. The few seconds gained are not worth that risk. Wait for the green, let traffic start moving, and then upgrade. Options A, B and D all push other drivers into an unsafe intersection or put the ambulance onto a sidewalk where pedestrians are.
questions.explanationZh: 在红灯前被车流围住时突然打开警灯警笛，会惊到无处可去的司机，其中有人会闯红灯冲进路口造成碰撞。这样抢到的几秒钟不值得冒这个险。正确做法是等绿灯亮、车流开始移动后再升级。A、B、D 都是把其他司机逼进不安全的路口，或者把救护车开上有行人的人行道。

questions.questionEn: An ambulance is transporting with lights and sirens and approaches an intersection where the light is red against it. What is the most appropriate way to proceed through the intersection?
questions.questionZh: 救护车正以灯笛模式转运，前方路口对本车方向是红灯。通过该路口最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Change the siren tone to attract attention and proceed through the intersection without slowing
options.zh: 切换警笛音调以引起注意，不减速直接通过路口

options.en: Slow and come to a complete stop, confirm that every lane of traffic has stopped and that the drivers have seen the ambulance, then proceed one lane at a time
options.zh: 减速并完全停车，确认每一条车道的车辆都已停下、司机确实看到了救护车，然后逐条车道通过

options.en: Come to a complete stop and wait until there is not a single other vehicle at the intersection before proceeding
options.zh: 完全停车，一直等到路口一辆其他车都没有时再通过

options.en: Switch the siren off while entering, so that drivers can hear the engine and the tires instead
options.zh: 进入路口时关掉警笛，让司机能听见发动机和轮胎的声音

questions.explanationEn: Emergency lights and sirens request the right of way; they do not grant it. Intersections are where most ambulance collisions happen, so the driver stops, clears each lane individually, and moves only when the traffic in that lane has visibly stopped. Option C uses an absolute ('not a single vehicle') that cannot be achieved in real traffic, and absolute wording in an option is usually the sign of a wrong answer. A and D both remove the warning that other drivers depend on.
questions.explanationZh: 警灯和警笛只是请求路权，并不等于获得路权；路口是救护车碰撞最集中的地方。司机要停车、逐条车道确认，只有当那条车道的车辆明显停下后才通过。C 用了「一辆车都没有」这种绝对化措辞，在真实车流中根本做不到——选项里出现绝对化措辞，通常就是错误答案的标志。A 和 D 则取消了其他司机赖以察觉救护车的警示。

questions.questionEn: While responding with lights and sirens, an ambulance reaches an intersection controlled by a stop sign facing the ambulance. What must the driver do?
questions.questionZh: 救护车以灯笛模式出勤，到达一个本车方向设有停车标志（Stop Sign）的路口。司机必须怎么做？

options.en: Come to a complete stop, then proceed only once it has been confirmed to be safe
options.zh: 完全停车，确认安全之后再通过

options.en: Slow to walking speed without stopping, which satisfies the requirement during an emergency response
options.zh: 减速到步行速度但不停车，紧急出勤时这样就满足要求

options.en: Proceed without stopping, because emergency status exempts the ambulance from stop signs
options.zh: 不停车直接通过，因为紧急状态使救护车不受停车标志约束

options.en: Proceed without stopping as long as no pedestrians are visible on the corners
options.zh: 只要路口拐角看不到行人，就可以不停车通过

questions.explanationEn: The emergency-vehicle exemptions in provincial motor vehicle law do not remove the duty to drive with due care. A complete stop is required, and the ambulance proceeds only when the driver has confirmed the way is clear. Options B, C and D all treat the exemption as permission to enter blind, and 'no pedestrians visible' is not the same thing as 'no pedestrians' — the vehicle or person you cannot see is still there.
questions.explanationZh: 省级机动车法规给予紧急车辆的豁免并不免除谨慎驾驶的义务：必须完全停车，司机确认道路通畅后才能通过。B、C、D 都把豁免当成了盲目进入路口的许可，而且「看不到行人」不等于「没有行人」——你看不见的车和人依然在那里。

questions.questionEn: Paramedics are transporting a 34-year-old patient with an isolated, splinted forearm fracture. Pain is controlled, vital signs are normal, and the hospital is 20 minutes away. The partner suggests running lights and sirens to shorten the trip. What is the most appropriate decision?
questions.questionZh: 救护员正在转运一名 34 岁患者，单纯前臂骨折已夹板固定，疼痛已控制，生命体征正常，距医院 20 分钟车程。搭档建议开灯笛以缩短路程时间。最恰当的决定是什么？

options.en: Use lights and sirens, because arriving sooner always improves patient outcome
options.zh: 使用灯笛，因为到得越早患者预后总是越好

options.en: Use lights and sirens, because the patient's pain is suffering and justifies an emergency response
options.zh: 使用灯笛，因为疼痛本身就是痛苦，足以构成紧急转运的理由

options.en: Use the lights only without the siren, which removes the risk of an emergency response
options.zh: 只开警灯不拉警笛，这样就消除了紧急出勤的风险

options.en: Transport at routine status, because lights and sirens typically save only a few minutes while sharply increasing the risk of a collision
options.zh: 以普通状态转运，因为灯笛通常只能省下几分钟，却显著增加碰撞风险

questions.explanationEn: Emergency driving is an intervention with real risk: collisions injure crews, patients and the public, and studies of urban transport show the time saved is usually only a couple of minutes. It is justified only when those minutes would change the outcome. This patient is splinted, comfortable and stable, and nothing about the trip is time-critical. The word 'always' in option A is the giveaway. Option C is wrong because lights without a siren still encourages the driver to take risks while giving other drivers less warning, not more.
questions.explanationZh: 紧急驾驶本身是一种带真实风险的处置——碰撞会伤到机组、患者和路人——而城市转运的研究显示灯笛通常只省下两三分钟，只有当这几分钟能改变结局时才值得。这名患者已固定、无痛、稳定，行程中没有任何时间敏感因素。A 里的「总是」就是破绽。C 也不对：只开警灯并不会降低风险，司机照样会冒险，而其他车辆得到的警示反而更少。

questions.questionEn: During a routine-status transport, a 62-year-old patient with chest pain suddenly becomes unresponsive, apneic and pulseless. The ambulance is ten minutes from the hospital on a busy highway. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 一次普通状态转运途中，一名 62 岁胸痛患者突然失去反应、呼吸停止、无脉搏。救护车正行驶在繁忙的高速公路上，距医院还有 10 分钟。最恰当的处置是什么？

options.en: Continue driving at increased speed while the attending paramedic performs chest compressions standing beside the stretcher
options.zh: 继续加速行驶，由随车救护员站在担架旁做胸外按压

options.en: Have the driver pull over and stop in a safe location so that the crew can deliver high-quality CPR and defibrillate, and request additional resources
options.zh: 让司机在安全地点靠边停车，机组做高质量心肺复苏并除颤，同时请求增援

options.en: Continue driving and radio the hospital to have a resuscitation team meet the ambulance at the door
options.zh: 继续行驶，同时用电台通知医院派复苏团队在门口接车

options.en: Turn around and return to the scene, where there is more room to work
options.zh: 掉头返回现场，那里空间更大便于抢救

questions.explanationEn: Chest compressions delivered in a moving ambulance are shallow and frequently interrupted, and the compressor cannot be restrained: every corner and every brake application degrades the compressions and endangers the crew member. Survival from cardiac arrest depends on compression quality and early defibrillation, not on arrival time — the ambulance is a transport platform, not a resuscitation bay. Stop somewhere safe, work the arrest properly, and call for more hands. Option C accepts ten minutes of poor CPR in exchange for a waiting team.
questions.explanationZh: 在行驶中的救护车里做胸外按压，深度不够、中断频繁，而且按压者无法系安全带：每一次转弯和刹车都会破坏按压质量并危及这名机组人员。心脏骤停的存活率取决于按压质量和早期除颤，而不是到院时间——救护车是运输平台，不是复苏室。正确做法是找安全地点停车、认真抢救并呼叫增援。C 等于用十分钟的劣质复苏，去换医院门口一支等着的团队。

questions.questionEn: Responding to a call, an ambulance meets traffic backed up in both directions on a two-lane road. The driver considers crossing the centre line to pass the stopped vehicles. Which statement describes the correct approach?
questions.questionZh: 救护车出勤途中，遇到一条双车道公路两个方向都堵死。司机考虑越过中线，从停住的车辆旁边借道通过。以下哪项描述了正确做法？

options.en: Cross into the oncoming lane at normal speed, because the emergency lights give the ambulance the right of way
options.zh: 以正常速度驶入对向车道，因为警灯已经赋予救护车路权

options.en: Never cross the centre line under any circumstances while operating an ambulance
options.zh: 驾驶救护车时在任何情况下都绝不能越过中线

options.en: Cross only when the road ahead is clearly visible for the entire manoeuvre, at greatly reduced speed, and when there is no safe alternative route
options.zh: 只有在整个借道过程视线全程通畅、大幅减速、且没有其他安全路线可走时才能越线

options.en: Cross at the crest of a hill, because oncoming drivers will see the emergency lights before they see the ambulance itself
options.zh: 在坡顶越线，因为对向司机会先看到警灯，再看到车本身

questions.explanationEn: Driving against the flow of traffic removes every assumption the other drivers are making, so it is a last resort: done slowly, only where the sight line covers the whole manoeuvre, and only where there is a gap to return to your own lane. Option D is a real and lethal error — a hill crest or a curve is exactly where neither driver has a sight line and the oncoming driver has no time to react. Option B is an absolute in the other direction: the manoeuvre is permitted, it is simply tightly conditioned. Option A confuses requesting the right of way with having it.
questions.explanationZh: 逆向行驶推翻了其他司机做出的一切预判，因此只能作为最后手段：低速通过，必须看得见整段路，而且要有能回到本方车道的空当。D 是真实而致命的错误——坡顶和弯道恰恰是双方都没有视线、对向司机来不及反应的地方。B 则是另一个方向上的绝对化：这个动作是允许的，只是条件极严。A 把「请求路权」误当成「拥有路权」。

questions.questionEn: An ambulance responding with lights and sirens must pass through an active school zone at dismissal time. What is the correct practice?
questions.questionZh: 救护车以灯笛模式出勤，途中必须穿过一个正在放学的学校区。正确做法是什么？

options.en: Reduce speed and pass with heightened caution, because children may not react to lights and sirens the way adult drivers and pedestrians do
options.zh: 减速并格外谨慎地通过，因为儿童对警灯警笛的反应不像成年司机和行人那样可预测

options.en: Maintain the response speed, because emergency status suspends the school zone speed limit
options.zh: 保持出勤速度，因为紧急状态已经解除了学校区的限速

options.en: Increase the siren volume so that the children clear the roadway faster
options.zh: 加大警笛音量，让孩子们更快离开路面

options.en: Switch off the lights and siren so that children are not drawn toward the ambulance
options.zh: 关掉警灯和警笛，以免把孩子吸引过来

questions.explanationEn: Children are the least predictable pedestrians on the road — some freeze, some run toward the ambulance, and some run away from it into traffic — and a school zone at dismissal also contains stopped buses and distracted parents. Slowing down costs seconds; striking a child does not have a recoverable cost. Option B is false: emergency exemptions never suspend the duty of due care in school and playground zones. Option C treats noise as crowd control, and option D removes the warning that the surrounding drivers need.
questions.explanationZh: 儿童是道路上最难预测的行人——有的会僵住，有的会朝救护车跑过来，有的会慌乱跑进车流；放学时段的学校区里还有停靠的校车和分神的家长。减速损失的是几秒钟，撞到孩子则没有可以挽回的代价。B 是错的：紧急豁免从不解除学校区和游乐区的谨慎义务。C 把噪音当成疏散手段，D 则拿掉了周围司机需要的警示。

questions.questionEn: An ambulance responding with lights and sirens reaches a construction zone where a flagger is controlling single-lane alternating traffic and is holding the STOP paddle toward the ambulance. What should the driver do?
questions.questionZh: 救护车以灯笛模式出勤，到达一处施工区。持牌员正在指挥单车道交替通行，并把「STOP」牌面朝救护车。司机应该怎么做？

options.en: Proceed past the flagger, because the emergency call takes priority over construction traffic control
options.zh: 越过持牌员继续行驶，因为紧急任务优先于施工交通管制

options.en: Use the shoulder to bypass the flagger and the construction equipment
options.zh: 借用路肩绕过持牌员和施工机械

options.en: Sound the air horn continuously until the flagger waves the ambulance through
options.zh: 持续鸣气笛，直到持牌员挥手放行

options.en: Slow and stop as directed, and proceed only when the flagger signals that it is safe
options.zh: 减速并按指示停车，等持牌员示意安全后再通过

questions.explanationEn: The flagger is the only person who knows what is happening in the closed lane — whether oncoming traffic has already been released, whether a loader is reversing, whether there is an open trench. Heavy equipment operators wear hearing protection inside a loud cab and will not hear a siren. Make your presence known, then follow the flagger's direction; they will usually clear you within seconds. Passing without permission is how ambulances end up in head-on collisions inside coned-off lanes, and option B adds soft shoulders and workers on foot to the problem.
questions.explanationZh: 持牌员是唯一知道封闭车道里正在发生什么的人——对向车流是否已经放行、有没有正在倒车的装载机、前面有没有开挖的沟。重型机械操作员戴着护耳、坐在噪音很大的驾驶室里，根本听不见警笛。正确做法是让对方知道你在场，然后听指挥，通常几秒钟就会被放行。未经许可强行通过，正是救护车在锥桶封闭车道里发生正面碰撞的原因；B 还额外引入了松软路肩和步行工人的风险。

questions.questionEn: An ambulance is transporting a patient on a highway during heavy rain. Which adjustment to driving technique is most important?
questions.questionZh: 救护车在大雨中沿高速公路转运患者。以下哪项驾驶调整最重要？

options.en: Keep the normal following distance, because ambulance braking systems are engineered for the vehicle's weight
options.zh: 保持正常跟车距离，因为救护车的制动系统本来就是按整车重量设计的

options.en: Reduce speed and increase the following distance, because braking distance lengthens on wet pavement and the ambulance's high centre of gravity makes an emergency swerve likely to cause a rollover
options.zh: 降低车速并加大跟车距离，因为湿路面上制动距离显著变长，而救护车重心高，紧急变线极易导致侧翻

options.en: Increase speed so that the total time spent driving in hazardous conditions is reduced
options.zh: 提高车速，以缩短在恶劣条件下行驶的总时间

options.en: Switch the siren off so that the driver can concentrate on reading the road surface
options.zh: 关掉警笛，让司机能专心观察路面

questions.explanationEn: A loaded ambulance is a tall, heavy box with its mass carried high. On wet pavement it needs far more distance to stop, and it cannot change direction quickly without the risk of tipping. The correct response to reduced traction is to buy distance and time: slow down and open the gap so that no situation ever requires a sudden swerve. Option C is the 'least time exposed' fallacy — risk climbs far faster than exposure time falls.
questions.explanationZh: 满载的救护车是又高又重、重量集中在上部的箱式车：湿路面上停车距离大大加长，而且无法快速变向，否则有翻车风险。附着力变差时的正确应对是为自己争取距离和时间——减速、拉开车距，让任何情况都不需要靠猛打方向来化解。C 是典型的「缩短暴露时间」谬误：风险上升的速度远快于暴露时间下降的速度。

questions.questionEn: What following distance should an ambulance driver maintain behind the vehicle ahead in good road conditions?
questions.questionZh: 路况良好时，救护车司机与前车之间应保持多大的跟车距离？

options.en: One vehicle length for every 10 km/h of speed
options.zh: 车速每 10 公里/小时对应一个车身长度

options.en: Two seconds, the same interval used for a passenger car
options.zh: 两秒，与普通轿车相同

options.en: At least four seconds, increased further in rain or snow, on downgrades, and when the vehicle is heavily loaded
options.zh: 至少四秒，遇到雨雪、下坡和重载时还要进一步加大

options.en: Whatever gap is small enough to stop other drivers from merging into it
options.zh: 保持小到别的车插不进来的间距

questions.explanationEn: An ambulance weighs several times what a car does and needs correspondingly longer to stop, so the two-second rule that works for a car is not enough; four seconds is the usual minimum, extended for weather, load and grade. Option D is the error crews genuinely make — drivers close the gap out of frustration when cars keep merging into it, and that is exactly how a rear-end collision happens with a patient on board. Option A is a rule of thumb that does not scale with the vehicle's mass.
questions.explanationZh: 救护车的重量是轿车的数倍，制动距离也相应更长，所以适用于轿车的两秒法则并不够；通常以四秒为最低标准，遇到天气、载重和坡度还要加长。D 是机组现实中真会犯的错——司机因为总有车插进来而烦躁地压缩车距，而这正是车上载着患者时发生追尾的原因。A 这类经验口诀没有随车重变化。

questions.questionEn: Before loading a patient, the crew must back the ambulance down a narrow, unlit driveway to reach the residence. What is the correct procedure?
questions.questionZh: 装载患者之前，机组需要把救护车倒进一条狭窄且没有照明的私家车道才能到达住宅。正确做法是什么？

options.en: Back up slowly using the mirrors and the reversing camera
options.zh: 借助后视镜和倒车影像慢慢倒车

options.en: Back up quickly, to minimize the time the ambulance blocks the roadway
options.zh: 快速倒车，尽量缩短救护车占用道路的时间

options.en: Ask a bystander standing nearby to direct the ambulance
options.zh: 请旁边的路人帮忙指挥倒车

options.en: Stop, have the partner get out and act as a guide at the rear, remaining visible in the driver's mirror throughout the manoeuvre
options.zh: 停车，让搭档下车到车尾担任引导员，全程保持在司机后视镜可见范围内

questions.explanationEn: Reversing accounts for a large share of ambulance collisions and almost all of them are preventable. The standard is a trained guide at the rear — not a camera, not a bystander — and the guide must stay in the driver's mirror at all times: if the driver loses sight of the guide, the driver stops. Mirrors and cameras have blind zones large enough to hide a child, a low post or a curb cut. Option C hands the responsibility to someone with no training and no accountability.
questions.explanationZh: 倒车造成了救护车碰撞事故中的很大一部分，而这些几乎都可以避免。标准做法是由受过训练的搭档在车尾引导——不是靠摄像头，也不是靠路人——并且引导员必须全程出现在司机的后视镜里：一旦司机看不见引导员，就立即停车。摄像头和后视镜都有盲区，足以藏下一个孩子、一根矮柱或一处路缘豁口。C 把责任交给了既没受过训练也不承担责任的人。

questions.questionEn: Where should the attending paramedic be positioned during transport of a patient who requires monitoring but no active intervention?
questions.questionZh: 转运一名只需监护、暂时不需要主动处置的患者时，随车救护员应处于什么位置？

options.en: In the attendant (airway) seat with the shoulder harness and lap belt fastened
options.zh: 坐在随车员座椅（气道位）上，系好肩带和腰带

options.en: On the squad bench unrestrained, so that the patient can be reached immediately
options.zh: 不系安全带坐在侧长凳上，以便随时够到患者

options.en: Standing beside the stretcher, holding the grab rail
options.zh: 站在担架旁，手扶扶手

options.en: Sitting on the edge of the stretcher beside the patient
options.zh: 坐在担架边缘，紧挨患者

questions.explanationEn: The attendant seat exists because it is the position in the patient compartment that is crash-tested with a restraint system while still allowing head-to-toe access to the patient. An unrestrained provider in the patient compartment is thrown into cabinets, into the patient, or through the bulkhead in a collision, and unrestrained crew injuries are among the most severe in this occupation. If a task genuinely cannot be performed while restrained, the correct answer is to ask the driver to stop — not to unbuckle while the vehicle is moving.
questions.explanationZh: 随车员座椅之所以存在，是因为它是患者舱里既通过碰撞测试、配有约束系统，又能让人从头到脚接触患者的座位。碰撞时未系安全带的救护员会被甩向柜体、患者，甚至穿过隔断，而未系约束的机组伤害是这一行里最严重的伤害之一。如果某项操作确实无法在系着安全带的状态下完成，正确答案是请司机停车，而不是在行驶中解开安全带。

questions.questionEn: How should an adult patient be secured to the stretcher for transport?
questions.questionZh: 转运成人患者时，应如何把患者固定在担架上？

options.en: A single chest strap is sufficient for an alert, cooperative patient
options.zh: 对清醒配合的患者，胸前系一条约束带就够了

options.en: Three body straps plus the shoulder harness system, with the stretcher locked into its floor mount
options.zh: 三条身体约束带加肩部约束系统，同时担架锁进地板固定座

options.en: Body straps only; the shoulder harness is used for paediatric patients
options.zh: 只用身体约束带；肩部约束是给儿科患者用的

options.en: Locking the stretcher into its mount is sufficient, because the mount absorbs the crash forces
options.zh: 把担架锁进固定座就够了，因为碰撞力由固定座吸收

questions.explanationEn: The horizontal straps stop the patient sliding sideways or rolling off, but only the shoulder harness stops the patient being thrown forward off the head of the stretcher in a frontal collision — the most common form of serious ambulance crash. The stretcher mount protects the stretcher, not the person on it. All of these must be in place before the vehicle moves, including for the alert and cooperative patient, who has exactly the same inertia as anyone else.
questions.explanationZh: 横向约束带防止患者侧滑或滚落，但只有肩部约束才能在正面碰撞——也就是救护车最常见的严重事故形式——中防止患者从担架头端被甩出去。担架固定座保护的是担架，不是担架上的人。车辆起步前这些约束都必须到位，对清醒配合的患者同样如此，因为惯性对谁都一样。

questions.questionEn: Why must the cardiac monitor, the drug bag and the portable oxygen cylinder be secured in their mounts before the ambulance moves?
questions.questionZh: 为什么救护车起步前必须把心电监护仪、药箱和便携氧气瓶固定在各自的支架里？

options.en: To keep the compartment tidy for routine equipment inspections
options.zh: 为了让车厢整洁，便于例行装备检查

options.en: To prevent the equipment from being stolen while the doors are open at the hospital
options.zh: 为了防止在医院开门时被人偷走

options.en: To stop the batteries from discharging while the vehicle is in motion
options.zh: 为了防止行驶过程中电池放电

options.en: Because in a collision or during hard braking, unsecured items become projectiles that can strike the crew and the patient
options.zh: 因为碰撞或急刹时，未固定的物品会变成飞行物砸向机组和患者

questions.explanationEn: A 10 kg monitor travelling at highway speed strikes with the force of a small motorcycle, and a loose oxygen cylinder is worse still — if the valve shears off, the cylinder becomes a missile that can go through the bulkhead. Everything in the patient compartment is either in a bracket, behind a latched cabinet door, or strapped down before the wheels turn. This is a check performed before every transport, not an occasional one.
questions.explanationZh: 一台 10 公斤的监护仪在高速行驶中撞过来，冲击力相当于一辆小型摩托车；散落的氧气瓶更危险，一旦阀门被剪断，气瓶就会变成能击穿隔断的导弹。患者舱里的每一件东西，在车轮转动之前都必须卡进支架、锁进柜门或绑好。这是每次转运前都要做的检查，不是偶尔为之。

questions.questionEn: A 58-year-old man with ongoing chest pain is on the third floor of a walk-up apartment building. The stairwell is narrow and turns 90 degrees at each landing. He is alert, his vital signs are stable, and he says he can walk down himself. What is the most appropriate way to move him to the ambulance?
questions.questionZh: 一名 58 岁男性持续胸痛，住在无电梯公寓三楼，楼梯狭窄、每个转角平台都是 90 度直角。他神志清楚，生命体征稳定，表示自己可以走下去。把他转移到救护车最恰当的方式是什么？

options.en: Let him walk down to the ambulance, since he is alert and this is by far the fastest option
options.zh: 让他自己走下楼，因为他神志清楚，而且这样明显最快

options.en: Carry him down on the wheeled stretcher with the two-person crew
options.zh: 由两人机组把他抬在轮式担架上下楼

options.en: Move him on a stair chair, requesting additional personnel so that the crew — not the patient — does all of the physical work
options.zh: 使用楼梯椅，并请求增派人手，让体力活全部由机组承担而不是由患者承担

options.en: Secure him to a long spine board and carry him down with the two-person crew
options.zh: 把他固定在长脊板上，由两人机组抬下楼

questions.explanationEn: Exertion in a patient with ongoing chest pain increases myocardial oxygen demand at precisely the moment the myocardium cannot meet it. The provincial guidelines direct crews to keep the patient at rest, avoid exertion during transfers, and bring the lifting and transfer devices to the patient. So walking is out, even though the patient offers and even though it is faster. The wheeled stretcher will not negotiate a narrow turning stairwell, and a long spine board is an extrication device that is uncomfortable and unnecessary in a patient with no trauma. The stair chair is designed for this stairwell; if two people are not enough, call for more.
questions.explanationZh: 持续胸痛的患者一活动，心肌耗氧就上升，而此刻心肌恰恰供不上。省考纲明确要求让患者休息、转移过程中避免用力，并把搬运和转移器材送到患者身边。所以即使患者主动提出、即使走下去更快，也不能让他走。轮式担架过不了狭窄的转角楼梯；长脊板是脱困器材，对没有创伤的患者既不舒服也无必要。楼梯椅正是为这种楼梯设计的，两个人不够就叫增援。

questions.questionEn: An air ambulance has landed at a scene landing zone. How should the ground crew approach the aircraft?
questions.questionZh: 空中救护直升机已在现场降落区着陆。地面机组应如何接近机身？

options.en: Wait for a signal from the flight crew, then approach from the front or the side within the pilot's field of view, in a crouch, keeping well away from the tail rotor
options.zh: 等待机组人员发出信号，再从机头或侧面、在飞行员视野内弯腰低姿接近，并远离尾桨

options.en: Approach from the rear, where the pilot can watch the crew in the mirrors
options.zh: 从机尾接近，这样飞行员可以通过后视镜看到机组

options.en: Approach as soon as the skids touch the ground, so that the patient transfer is not delayed
options.zh: 起落架一触地就上前，以免耽误患者交接

options.en: When the aircraft has landed on a slope, approach from the uphill side so that the crew stays in view
options.zh: 若直升机停在斜坡上，从坡上一侧接近，以便始终处于机组视野内

questions.explanationEn: The tail rotor is nearly invisible while turning and sits at head height on many airframes, so approaching the tail is the single most lethal error around a helicopter. Stay where the pilot can see you, wait to be waved in, and stay low, because the main rotor disc dips as it slows. Option C is wrong because the rotors are still at speed and the aircraft is not yet secured. Option D reverses the rule: on sloping ground the rotor disc is closest to the ground on the uphill side, so the approach is made from downhill and only when the flight crew signals.
questions.explanationZh: 尾桨旋转时几乎看不见，而且在很多机型上正好在头部高度——走向机尾是直升机周围最致命的一个错误。要待在飞行员看得见的位置，等对方招手示意再上前，并保持低姿，因为主旋翼在减速时会下垂。C 错在此时旋翼仍全速旋转、飞机尚未确认安全。D 则完全反了：停在斜坡上时，旋翼盘离地最近的一侧正是坡上一侧，所以必须从坡下一侧接近，而且要等机组示意。

questions.questionEn: Paramedics are asked to establish a landing zone for a helicopter at a rural scene. Which site is most suitable?
questions.questionZh: 救护员被要求在乡村现场设置直升机降落区。以下哪个场地最合适？

options.en: A paved parking lot roughly 15 by 15 metres, with overhead wires along one edge that the pilot should be able to see
options.zh: 约 15 米 × 15 米的柏油停车场，一侧上方有电线，但飞行员应该能看见

options.en: A gravel lot roughly 30 by 30 metres, flat and clear, marked with the crew's traffic cones set loose at the four corners
options.zh: 约 30 米 × 30 米、平整空旷的砾石场地，四角松放上机组随身的交通锥作标记

options.en: A firm, level field roughly 30 by 30 metres with a slope under about 5 degrees, clear of wires, poles, trees and loose debris, with unobstructed approach and departure paths
options.zh: 约 30 米 × 30 米、地面坚实平整、坡度小于约 5 度的场地，没有电线、电杆、树木和散落杂物，进场和离场航路无遮挡

options.en: Any flat area of at least 10 by 10 metres, since modern air ambulances are highly manoeuvrable
options.zh: 任何至少 10 米 × 10 米的平地，因为现代空中救护机机动性很强

questions.explanationEn: The working figure is roughly 30 by 30 metres of firm, level ground with no overhead obstruction and clear approach and departure paths. Slope matters because a steep site risks a rotor strike or a dynamic rollover. Wires are the classic killer and are almost impossible to see from the air, so a site with wires along one edge is not made safe by the pilot's eyesight. Loose cones, tarps and debris become projectiles in the rotor wash, so markers must be weighted or secured, and the size requirement is not negotiable downward.
questions.explanationZh: 通行标准是约 30 米 × 30 米、地面坚实平整、上方无遮挡、进离场航路通畅。坡度之所以重要，是因为坡度过大会导致旋翼触地或动态翻滚。电线是经典的致命因素，从空中几乎看不见，所以「飞行员应该能看见」并不能让一侧有电线的场地变安全。松放的交通锥、篷布和杂物在旋翼下洗气流中会变成飞行物，标记物必须压重或固定；尺寸要求也不能往下让步。

questions.questionEn: An ambulance is the first emergency vehicle to arrive at a two-vehicle collision in the through lanes of a highway at dusk. Fire and police are several minutes away. Where should the ambulance be parked?
questions.questionZh: 黄昏时分，一辆救护车最先到达高速公路行车道上的两车相撞现场，消防和警察还要几分钟才能到。救护车应该停在哪里？

options.en: Directly alongside the wreckage, to give the shortest carrying distance to the stretcher
options.zh: 直接停在残骸旁边，让抬担架的距离最短

options.en: Well past the wreckage in the direction of travel, so that traffic keeps flowing freely behind the crew
options.zh: 沿行驶方向停到残骸前方较远处，让身后的车流保持畅通

options.en: On the opposite shoulder, so that the crew can watch the approaching traffic while they work
options.zh: 停在对向路肩，方便机组一边工作一边观察来车

options.en: Upstream of the wreckage, angled so as to shield the working area, with warning lights on, accepting that this will obstruct traffic
options.zh: 停在残骸的上游（来车方向一侧），车身斜置以遮挡作业区，开启警示灯，并接受由此造成的交通阻塞

questions.explanationEn: Until a larger blocking apparatus arrives, the first unit on scene is the only barrier between approaching traffic and the people working in the live lanes. It is parked upstream and angled so that a vehicle which fails to stop strikes the ambulance rather than the crew. Obstructing traffic is the purpose here, not an unfortunate side effect — this is the case where the safest option is deliberately not the one that keeps the road moving. Once fire apparatus takes over the block, the ambulance repositions downstream so that it can leave without reversing. Option A leaves the crew fully exposed and option C sends them across live lanes carrying a patient.
questions.explanationZh: 在更大的阻挡车辆到达之前，第一辆到场的车是来车与活动车道上作业人员之间唯一的屏障：它要停在上游并斜置，使得万一有车没能刹住，撞上的是救护车而不是机组。阻塞交通在这里是目的，而不是不得已的副作用——这正是「最安全」与「让路面通畅」发生冲突、必须选最安全的情形。等消防车接手阻挡后，救护车再重新停到下游，以便离开时不必倒车。A 让机组完全暴露，C 则逼着机组带着患者横穿活动车道。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic has just given an intramuscular injection to an adult patient in the patient's living room. The vehicle's sharps container is in the ambulance parked outside. What should be done with the used needle?
questions.questionZh: 救护员刚在患者家的客厅给一名成年患者完成肌肉注射，车上的利器盒放在停在外面的救护车里。用过的针头应该怎么处理？

options.en: Recap the needle carefully and carry it out to the sharps container in the ambulance
options.zh: 小心地把针帽套回去，带到救护车上的利器盒里丢弃

options.en: Lay the uncapped needle on top of the drug bag until the crew packs up to leave
options.zh: 先把没盖帽的针头放在药箱上，等机组收拾东西离开时一起处理

options.en: Dispose of it immediately in the portable sharps container that was brought to the point of use
options.zh: 立即丢进随身带到操作现场的便携利器盒

options.en: Place it in the household garbage, since it was a single clean injection
options.zh: 丢进住户的生活垃圾，因为这只是一次干净的注射

questions.explanationEn: Sharps are disposed of at the point of use, immediately, by the person who used them, which is why a portable sharps container is carried in with the drug bag. Every step between using a needle and disposing of it is another chance to stick yourself, your partner, the patient or a member of the household. Recapping is a leading cause of needlestick injury, a needle 'parked' on a bag will eventually be grabbed by somebody, and household garbage exposes the family and the sanitation worker downstream.
questions.explanationZh: 利器必须由使用者在使用地点立即处置——这正是便携利器盒要跟着药箱一起带进现场的原因。从用完针到丢掉针，中间每多一个步骤，就多一次扎到自己、搭档、患者或家属的机会。回套针帽是针刺伤的首要原因；「暂放」在包上的针头迟早会被人抓到；丢进生活垃圾则会伤到家人和之后的清运工人。

questions.questionEn: While disposing of an IV catheter, a paramedic sustains a needlestick injury to the finger from a device that was used on a patient. What is the first action?
questions.questionZh: 救护员在丢弃静脉留置针时，被一支用过的针具刺伤手指。第一步应该做什么？

options.en: Wash the site immediately with soap and running water, then report the exposure and seek medical assessment
options.zh: 立即用肥皂和流动水冲洗伤口，然后上报暴露并接受医学评估

options.en: Notify the supervisor first, before doing anything to the wound
options.zh: 先通知主管，之后再处理伤口

options.en: Squeeze the wound to force blood out of it, then apply a bleach solution
options.zh: 挤压伤口把血挤出来，再涂抹漂白剂溶液

options.en: Finish the call, then wash the wound and report the injury at the end of the shift
options.zh: 先把这趟任务做完，下班时再清洗伤口并上报

questions.explanationEn: First aid comes first and it is simple: wash immediately and copiously with soap and running water, then report and get assessed. Reporting matters enormously, but it comes second because a few minutes' delay in reporting costs nothing operationally while washing is time-critical. Squeezing the wound and applying caustics such as bleach damages tissue and has never been shown to reduce transmission. Waiting until the end of shift can push the exposed worker past the window in which post-exposure prophylaxis is most effective.
questions.explanationZh: 先做急救，而且方法很简单：立即用肥皂和流动水大量冲洗，然后上报并接受评估。上报非常重要，但排在冲洗之后，因为晚几分钟上报没有任何运行代价，而冲洗有时效性。挤压伤口、涂抹漂白剂这类腐蚀性液体会损伤组织，从未被证明能降低感染传播。拖到下班再处理，可能错过暴露后预防用药最有效的时间窗。

questions.questionEn: After a significant blood exposure, how soon should the paramedic be medically assessed?
questions.questionZh: 发生有意义的血液暴露后，救护员应在多久之内接受医学评估？

options.en: Within 30 days, which is the reporting window for a workplace injury claim
options.zh: 30 天之内，这是工伤申报的时限

options.en: At the next scheduled occupational health appointment
options.zh: 等到下一次已经排好的职业健康随访

options.en: Only if the source patient is later confirmed to be HIV positive
options.zh: 只有在后来确认源患者 HIV 阳性时才需要

options.en: As soon as possible, ideally within one to two hours, because post-exposure prophylaxis becomes less effective the longer it is delayed
options.zh: 尽快，最好在一到两小时之内，因为暴露后预防用药拖得越久效果越差

questions.explanationEn: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis is a time-critical treatment: it works best when started within hours, and its benefit falls off steeply after that, so an exposed provider goes to the emergency department or occupational health right away rather than at a convenient time. The source patient's status is usually unknown in that window and cannot be waited for. Workers' compensation reporting deadlines run on a separate and much longer clock, and must not be confused with the clinical one.
questions.explanationZh: HIV 暴露后预防是有时效的治疗：数小时内启动效果最好，之后获益迅速下降，所以发生暴露的人员要立刻去急诊或职业健康部门，而不是挑方便的时间。源患者的感染状态在这个时间窗里往往还不清楚，不能等结果。工伤申报的时限是另一套、长得多的时间表，绝不能和临床时限混为一谈。

questions.questionEn: While suctioning a bleeding airway, a paramedic who is not wearing eye protection receives a splash of blood in the eye. What should be done?
questions.questionZh: 救护员在为一名气道出血的患者做吸引时没有佩戴护目装备，血液溅入眼内。应该怎么处理？

options.en: Rub the eye first to clear any visible debris, then irrigate it
options.zh: 先揉眼把看得见的异物弄出来，再冲洗

options.en: Irrigate the eye immediately with water or normal saline for 15 to 20 minutes, then report the exposure and seek assessment
options.zh: 立即用清水或生理盐水持续冲洗眼睛 15 到 20 分钟，然后上报暴露并接受评估

options.en: Apply an antibiotic ointment to the eye and continue with patient care
options.zh: 涂抗生素眼膏，继续照护患者

options.en: Wait until arrival at hospital and have the emergency department irrigate it
options.zh: 等到医院后由急诊科冲洗

questions.explanationEn: Mucous membranes are a genuine route of transmission for bloodborne pathogens, and the treatment is immediate, prolonged irrigation — on scene, with whatever clean water or saline is at hand, for a full 15 to 20 minutes rather than a token rinse. Rubbing drives contaminant into the conjunctiva and abrades it. Ointment does nothing against a viral exposure. Deferring irrigation to hospital wastes the window in which dilution actually helps. This is also the item to recall when deciding whether eye protection is worth putting on for a suctioning call.
questions.explanationZh: 黏膜是血源性病原体的真实传播途径，处理方式就是立即、长时间冲洗——在现场用手边任何干净的水或生理盐水，足足冲 15 到 20 分钟，而不是象征性地冲一下。揉眼会把污染物揉进结膜并擦伤黏膜；眼膏对病毒暴露毫无作用；把冲洗拖到医院则浪费了稀释真正有效的那个时间窗。这道题也提醒：在决定吸引操作要不要戴护目装备时，代价是什么。

questions.questionEn: Which situation requires a fit-tested N95 respirator rather than a procedure (surgical) mask?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪种情况需要佩戴经过密合度测试的 N95 呼吸器，而不是普通医用外科口罩？

options.en: Transporting a patient with weight loss, night sweats and a chronic productive cough in whom active pulmonary tuberculosis is suspected
options.zh: 转运一名有体重下降、盗汗、慢性咳痰、怀疑活动性肺结核的患者

options.en: Assisting a patient who has an anterior nosebleed
options.zh: 处理一名前鼻出血的患者

options.en: Any patient contact during the influenza season
options.zh: 流感季节内的任何患者接触

options.en: Cleaning the patient compartment after a routine interfacility transfer
options.zh: 完成一次常规院间转运后清洁患者舱

questions.explanationEn: An N95 filters airborne particles and only works if it seals to the face, which is why fit testing exists. It is indicated for suspected airborne diseases — tuberculosis, measles, varicella — and for aerosol-generating procedures. A procedure mask blocks droplets and splash, which covers a nosebleed and ordinary respiratory illness. Wearing an N95 for every contact is not extra protection; it is a way to exhaust the supply and to wear them carelessly. Cleaning calls for gloves and, if splash is likely, eye protection.
questions.explanationZh: N95 过滤的是空气传播的微粒，而且只有与面部密合才有效，这正是要做密合度测试的原因。它适用于怀疑经空气传播的疾病（结核、麻疹、水痘）以及会产生气溶胶的操作。普通外科口罩阻挡的是飞沫和喷溅，足以应付鼻出血和普通呼吸道感染。每次接触都戴 N95 并不会更安全，只会让库存耗尽、佩戴变得随便。清洁作业需要的是手套，必要时加护目装备。

questions.questionEn: On which of the following calls should the crew put on a gown and face shield in addition to gloves?
questions.questionZh: 以下哪一趟任务中，机组除了手套之外还应穿隔离衣、戴面屏？

options.en: A patient with chest pain who needs a 12-lead ECG
options.zh: 需要做 12 导联心电图的胸痛患者

options.en: A lift assist for a patient who has slipped out of a chair and is uninjured
options.zh: 从椅子上滑落但没有受伤、只需协助搬起的患者

options.en: An imminent childbirth with the mother crowning
options.zh: 胎头已经着冠、即将分娩的产妇

options.en: A stable patient with a swollen, painful ankle after twisting it
options.zh: 崴脚后踝关节肿痛、病情稳定的患者

questions.explanationEn: Personal protective equipment is chosen according to what the task is likely to spray or soak, not according to how sick the patient is. A delivery reliably produces amniotic fluid and blood at close range and at speed, so the gown and face protection go on before the crew is committed to the task. The other three calls involve no anticipated splash and gloves are sufficient. The same reasoning selects gown and face shield for major haemorrhage, active vomiting, suctioning and intubation.
questions.explanationZh: 个人防护装备的选择依据是这项操作可能喷溅或浸湿什么，而不是患者病得有多重。接生几乎必然会在近距离、高速度地产生羊水和血液，所以隔离衣和面部防护要在投入操作之前就穿戴好。另外三种情况都没有可预期的喷溅，戴手套就足够。同样的判断也适用于大出血、剧烈呕吐、吸引和插管。

questions.questionEn: After caring for a patient with an infectious diarrhoeal illness, which item of personal protective equipment is removed first?
questions.questionZh: 照护一名感染性腹泻患者之后，脱卸个人防护装备时最先脱哪一件？

options.en: The eye protection
options.zh: 护目装备

options.en: The gloves
options.zh: 手套

options.en: The gown
options.zh: 隔离衣

options.en: The respirator or mask
options.zh: 呼吸器或口罩

questions.explanationEn: Doffing runs from the most contaminated item to the least. The gloves have touched everything, so they come off first and hand hygiene follows immediately; eye protection and gown come next; and the mask or respirator is removed last, outside the contaminated area, because the front of it must never be touched by a contaminated hand. Taking the mask off first means removing it with dirty gloves and putting that hand next to your own eyes, nose and mouth.
questions.explanationZh: 脱卸顺序遵循「从最脏到最干净」。手套接触过所有东西，所以最先脱，脱完立即做手卫生；接着是护目装备和隔离衣；口罩或呼吸器最后脱，而且要在污染区之外脱，因为它的正面绝不能被污染的手碰到。先脱口罩意味着用脏手套去摘，把那只手放到自己的眼、鼻、口旁边。

questions.questionEn: What must be done after removing gloves?
questions.questionZh: 脱下手套之后必须做什么？

options.en: Nothing further, provided the gloves did not tear during the call
options.zh: 不用再做什么，只要这趟任务中手套没有破损

options.en: Nothing further, provided a new pair of gloves is put on right away
options.zh: 不用再做什么，只要马上换上一副新手套

options.en: Hand hygiene, but only if the patient was known to have an infectious disease
options.zh: 做手卫生，但只在已知患者患有传染病时才需要

options.en: Hand hygiene every time, because gloves can have unnoticed defects and the hands are contaminated during removal
options.zh: 每次都要做手卫生，因为手套可能有肉眼看不到的破损，而且脱手套的过程本身就会污染双手

questions.explanationEn: Gloves are not a substitute for hand hygiene and never have been. Microscopic perforations are common, and even an intact glove transfers organisms onto the hands as it is peeled off — this is the most consistently missed moment in prehospital infection control. Hands are cleaned after every glove removal, regardless of what the patient had, and cleaned again before the next patient contact.
questions.explanationZh: 手套从来不能替代手卫生。手套上出现微小穿孔很常见；即使手套完好，脱下的动作也会把微生物带到手上——这是院前感染控制中最常被跳过的一个环节。无论患者得的是什么病，每次脱手套后都要做手卫生，下一次接触患者前再做一次。

questions.questionEn: Wearing gloves, the crew has just moved an 80-year-old patient from her bed onto the stretcher. The next task is to start an intravenous line. What should be done before the IV is started?
questions.questionZh: 机组刚戴着手套把一名 80 岁女性患者从床上转移到担架上，下一步要建立静脉通路。开始扎针之前应该做什么？

options.en: Remove the gloves, perform hand hygiene, and put on a clean pair of gloves
options.zh: 脱掉手套、做手卫生，再戴上一副干净手套

options.en: Wipe the outside of the gloves with an alcohol swab and continue with the same pair
options.zh: 用酒精棉片擦拭手套外面，继续用这一副

options.en: Continue with the same gloves, since it is the same patient
options.zh: 继续用这一副手套，因为还是同一个患者

options.en: Continue with the same gloves and perform hand hygiene once the call is finished
options.zh: 继续用这一副手套，等这趟任务结束后再做手卫生

questions.explanationEn: Hand hygiene is required between a dirty task and a clean one on the same patient, not only between patients. Gloves that have handled bedding, skin and a transfer are now carrying the patient's own skin flora directly to a site you are about to puncture. Disinfecting the outside of gloves is not an accepted practice: it degrades the glove material and does nothing about the hands inside them.
questions.explanationZh: 在同一名患者身上，从「脏」操作转到「净」操作之间同样需要做手卫生，而不只是换患者时才做。刚接触过床品、皮肤和搬运的手套，正把患者自身的皮肤菌群直接带到你即将穿刺的部位。擦拭手套外表面不是被认可的做法：它会破坏手套材质，也解决不了手套里面那双手的问题。

questions.questionEn: When must the hands be washed with soap and running water rather than cleaned with an alcohol-based hand rub?
questions.questionZh: 什么情况下必须用肥皂和流动水洗手，而不能只用含酒精的免洗手消毒剂？

options.en: Always — alcohol-based hand rub is never adequate in the prehospital setting
options.zh: 任何时候都必须洗手——院前环境下免洗手消毒剂从来都不够

options.en: Only when hand hygiene is being performed inside a hospital
options.zh: 只有在医院内部做手卫生时才需要

options.en: When the hands are visibly soiled, and after caring for a patient with suspected Clostridioides difficile or norovirus
options.zh: 双手有肉眼可见污染时，以及照护疑似艰难梭菌或诺如病毒感染的患者之后

options.en: Whenever gloves have been worn during the call
options.zh: 只要这趟任务中戴过手套就必须洗手

questions.explanationEn: Alcohol-based rub is the default in the field: it is faster, more accessible and more effective against most organisms. What it does not do is remove visible soil, and it does not kill spores or non-enveloped viruses, so C. difficile and norovirus require soap and water with mechanical washing. Option A is an absolute that contradicts current practice, option B confuses the setting with the indication, and option D would rule out the rub on essentially every call.
questions.explanationZh: 在院前环境中含酒精免洗手消毒剂是首选：更快、更易获得，对大多数微生物也更有效。它做不到的是去除肉眼可见的污染，也杀不死芽孢和无包膜病毒，所以艰难梭菌和诺如病毒必须用肥皂和流动水做机械性洗手。A 是与现行做法相悖的绝对化表述，B 把场所和指征混为一谈，D 则等于把免洗消毒剂在几乎每趟任务中都排除掉。

questions.questionEn: A crew has completed four transports this shift. Which one requires the patient compartment to be taken out of service for a full disinfection, rather than the routine end-of-call surface wipe-down?
questions.questionZh: 机组这个班已经完成四趟转运。其中哪一趟之后必须把患者舱停用做彻底消毒，而不是仅做每趟结束后的常规表面擦拭？

options.en: A patient with a stable ankle sprain who walked to the stretcher unassisted
options.zh: 踝关节扭伤、病情稳定、自己走到担架旁的患者

options.en: A patient with fever and a productive cough who was coughing throughout the transport, with a suspected febrile respiratory illness
options.zh: 发热、咳痰、全程咳嗽不止、怀疑发热性呼吸道疾病的患者

options.en: All four, because every transport requires a full disinfection of the compartment
options.zh: 四趟都要，因为每一次转运后都必须对患者舱做彻底消毒

options.en: A patient transported for an anxiety attack who was tearful but had no physical findings
options.zh: 因惊恐发作转运、有流泪但无阳性体征的患者

questions.explanationEn: The triggers for taking the compartment out of service and fully disinfecting it are specific: visible blood or body fluid contamination, a suspected febrile respiratory illness, suspected meningitis, and similar defined exposures. A patient who coughed throughout the transport with a suspected febrile respiratory illness meets that standard; a walking ankle sprain and an anxiety call do not. Option C is the absolute, and it is also the error crews make in the other direction — if everything requires a full decontamination, nothing gets one properly and the unit is never available.
questions.explanationZh: 把患者舱停用并做彻底消毒的触发条件是明确列出来的：肉眼可见的血液或体液污染、疑似发热性呼吸道疾病、疑似脑膜炎等特定暴露。全程咳嗽、怀疑发热性呼吸道疾病的患者符合这一标准；能走路的踝扭伤和惊恐发作则不符合。C 是绝对化选项，也正是机组在另一个方向上真会犯的错：如果什么都要彻底消毒，结果就是没有一次做得彻底，车辆还永远处于停用状态。

questions.questionEn: Which finding after a call obliges the crew to take the patient compartment out of service for a full disinfection?
questions.questionZh: 一趟任务结束后出现下列哪种情况时，机组必须把患者舱停用做彻底消毒？

options.en: The call lasted more than one hour
options.zh: 这趟任务持续超过一小时

options.en: The patient had a documented history of type 2 diabetes
options.zh: 患者有明确的 2 型糖尿病病史

options.en: The stretcher sheet was wrinkled and the pillow had been used
options.zh: 担架床单起皱、枕头被用过

options.en: Visible blood or other body fluid contamination on compartment surfaces or equipment
options.zh: 患者舱表面或器材上有肉眼可见的血液或其他体液污染

questions.explanationEn: Visible contamination is the clearest and least arguable trigger: anything the crew, the next patient or a cleaner could touch must be cleaned with an approved disinfectant before the unit returns to service. The duration of the call, the patient's chronic conditions and used linen are not contamination indicators — used linen is simply changed between every patient as a matter of routine.
questions.explanationZh: 肉眼可见的污染是最明确、最没有争议的触发条件：凡是机组、下一位患者或清洁人员可能触碰到的地方，在车辆恢复运行前都必须用核准的消毒剂清洁。任务时长、患者的慢性病史和用过的床品都不是污染指标——用过的床品只是每位患者之间例行更换而已。

questions.questionEn: A crew has transported a 17-year-old with fever, headache, neck stiffness and a purpuric rash. The receiving physician suspects meningococcal disease. What should the crew do with the ambulance?
questions.questionZh: 机组刚转运一名 17 岁患者，有发热、头痛、颈项强直和紫癜样皮疹，接诊医生怀疑脑膜炎球菌病。机组应该如何处理救护车？

options.en: Disinfect all contact surfaces with an approved disinfectant, keeping the surfaces wet for the full contact time stated on the label, and notify the health authority so that crew contact follow-up and prophylaxis can be arranged
options.zh: 用核准的消毒剂擦拭所有接触面，并让药液按标签规定的接触时间保持湿润，同时上报卫生部门，以便安排机组接触者随访和预防用药

options.en: Air the vehicle out with the doors open and return to service immediately
options.zh: 打开车门通风，随即恢复运行

options.en: Clean the stretcher, since that is the only surface the patient was in contact with
options.zh: 只清洁担架，因为那是患者唯一接触过的表面

options.en: Spray the disinfectant and wipe it off right away, so the surfaces dry quickly and the unit is available sooner
options.zh: 喷上消毒剂后马上擦干，让表面尽快变干、车辆更早可用

questions.explanationEn: Two things must both happen. The compartment is disinfected properly, and 'properly' means the surfaces stay visibly wet for the contact time the manufacturer specifies — usually several minutes. Wiping the product off immediately is the most common way a disinfection becomes nothing more than a wipe of clean-looking surfaces. Separately, close contact with meningococcal disease is a reportable occupational exposure: the crew may need chemoprophylaxis, and that only happens if somebody reports it. Cleaning the stretcher alone ignores the rails, the seats, the monitor and the door handles.
questions.explanationZh: 有两件事必须同时做到。第一，患者舱要正确消毒，而「正确」的含义是表面按厂家规定的接触时间保持可见的湿润，通常是几分钟；喷完立刻擦干，正是把一次消毒变成「只是把表面擦得好看」的最常见方式。第二，密切接触脑膜炎球菌病属于须上报的职业暴露：机组可能需要预防性用药，而这只有在有人上报后才会发生。只擦担架则忽略了扶手、座椅、监护仪和门把手。

questions.questionEn: An overturned tanker truck is leaking an unknown liquid across the roadway, and two people are reported down nearby. How should the crew approach?
questions.questionZh: 一辆罐车翻覆，不明液体正流过路面，据报附近有两人倒地。机组应如何接近？

options.en: Approach from downwind, so that the vapour blows back toward the tanker and away from the crew
options.zh: 从下风向接近，让蒸气吹回罐车方向、远离机组

options.en: Drive close enough to read the placard, then withdraw and report what it says
options.zh: 先把车开到能看清危险品标牌的距离，看清后再退回来上报

options.en: Approach from upwind and uphill, stop well back, read the placard with binoculars, and stage until hazmat declares the area safe
options.zh: 从上风向、地势高处接近，远远停下，用望远镜读取标牌，并在安全距离待命，等危化品处置队宣布安全

options.en: Enter the spill area to remove the patients, because they need care immediately
options.zh: 进入泄漏区把患者搬出来，因为他们急需救治

questions.explanationEn: Upwind and uphill, because vapour travels with the wind and heavier-than-air vapours and liquids run downhill. Distance is the only protective equipment a road ambulance carries. The placard is read from a distance with binoculars, never by driving up to it, because the contamination zone extends well beyond where the liquid is visible. Option D is the instinct that kills rescuers and creates more patients than it removes: a contaminated crew cannot treat anyone and will contaminate the ambulance and the emergency department as well. Option A reverses the rule entirely.
questions.explanationZh: 要走上风、走高处：蒸气随风扩散，比空气重的蒸气和液体则往低处流；对普通救护车来说，距离就是唯一的防护装备。危险品标牌要在远处用望远镜读，绝不能开近了看——污染区远远超出肉眼能看到液体的范围。D 是那种害死救援者的本能：被污染的机组既救不了人，还会污染救护车和急诊科，制造出比救出来更多的患者。A 则把规则完全弄反了。

questions.questionEn: Paramedics are dispatched to a reported stabbing. Police have not yet arrived. As the crew pulls up they can hear shouting and objects breaking inside the residence. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 救护员被派往一起报称的持刀伤人事件，警察尚未到场。机组停车时听到住宅内有人大喊大叫、有东西被砸碎。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Enter immediately, because survival from penetrating trauma depends on rapid transport
options.zh: 立即进入，因为穿透伤的存活率取决于尽快转运

options.en: Stage at a safe distance out of sight of the address and wait until police declare the scene safe
options.zh: 在看不到该住址的安全距离外待命，等警察宣布现场安全后再进入

options.en: Enter, but keep the stretcher between the crew and any aggressive person
options.zh: 进入，但始终把担架挡在机组和有攻击性的人之间

options.en: Knock on the door and announce that paramedics have arrived, in order to de-escalate the situation
options.zh: 敲门并大声表明救护员已到场，以缓和局势

questions.explanationEn: This is the sharpest form of the safe-versus-fast conflict, and the answer does not change: the fight is still in progress, the crew is unarmed and unarmoured, and a paramedic who becomes a patient adds a casualty while subtracting a rescuer. Stage where you cannot be seen from the address, keep the vehicle pointed out, and let police clear the scene. Announcing yourself does not de-escalate a fight in progress; it only tells everyone inside that another person has arrived. Option A states a real clinical truth and then draws the wrong conclusion from it, which is exactly how this trap is built.
questions.explanationZh: 这是「最安全 vs 最快」冲突最尖锐的形式，而答案不变：打斗还在进行，机组既没有武器也没有防护，一名变成患者的救护员既增加了一名伤者，又减少了一名救援者。正确做法是停在从住址看不见的位置、车头朝外待命，让警察先清场。表明身份并不能平息正在进行的打斗，只会告诉屋里所有人「又来了一个人」。A 陈述了一个真实的临床事实，却由此推出了错误的结论——这个陷阱正是这样搭起来的。

questions.questionEn: The crew arrives for a patient who has fallen in the back yard. A large dog is loose in the yard and is barking at the gate. What should the crew do?
questions.questionZh: 机组到场处理一名在后院摔倒的患者。院子里有一条大型犬没有拴住，正对着院门狂吠。机组应该怎么做？

options.en: Enter the yard and proceed with care, since most family dogs do not bite
options.zh: 小心进入院子继续工作，因为大多数家养犬不会咬人

options.en: Use the stretcher as a barrier to push the dog away from the working area
options.zh: 用担架当屏障，把狗挡开工作区域

options.en: Have one paramedic distract the dog while the other treats the patient
options.zh: 由一名救护员引开狗，另一名去处置患者

options.en: Ask the family to shut the dog inside the house or otherwise secure it away from the work area before entering
options.zh: 先请家属把狗关进屋里或以其他方式隔离到工作区域之外，再进入

questions.explanationEn: Dog bites are among the most common occupational injuries in this job, and a dog that is calm with its own family will often defend a frightened, injured owner against strangers who arrive and start touching them. The fix takes about fifteen seconds: ask the family to put the animal in a closed room. If nobody is available to secure the animal, that is a reason to wait for police or animal control — not a reason to improvise with equipment or to split the crew.
questions.explanationZh: 犬咬伤是这一行最常见的职业伤害之一；一条在自家人面前很温顺的狗，往往会在主人受伤、惊慌，而陌生人上前触碰时护主。解决办法只需大约十五秒：请家属把狗关进一个封闭房间。如果现场没有人能把狗控制住，那就是等警察或动物管制部门的理由，而不是用器材凑合或把机组拆散的理由。

questions.questionEn: A car has struck a utility pole and a live conductor is lying across the roof of the vehicle. The driver is conscious, appears uninjured, and is asking whether he should climb out. What should the crew tell him, and where should the crew stand?
questions.questionZh: 一辆汽车撞上电线杆，一根带电导线横搭在车顶上。司机清醒、看上去没有受伤，正在问自己是否应该爬出来。机组应该告诉他什么，机组自己又该站在哪里？

options.en: Tell him to stay inside the vehicle and not touch anything metal, and keep everyone at least one full pole span back until the utility confirms the line is de-energized
options.zh: 告诉他留在车内、不要触碰任何金属部件，同时所有人退到至少一整个电杆跨距之外，等供电公司确认线路已断电

options.en: Tell him to jump clear of the vehicle with both feet together and then shuffle away without lifting his feet
options.zh: 告诉他双脚并拢跳离车辆，然后双脚不离地地小步挪走

options.en: Move the conductor off the vehicle with a dry wooden pole or a branch, then open the door
options.zh: 先用干燥的木棍或树枝把导线从车上挑开，再打开车门

options.en: Approach and open the door while wearing the crew's disposable rubber examination gloves
options.zh: 戴上机组随身的一次性橡胶检查手套上前开门

questions.explanationEn: The vehicle body is carrying the current around the occupant, and the ground surrounding it may be energized in rings of decreasing voltage; stepping out bridges that gradient and can be fatal. So the patient stays put, and the crew stays back at least the distance between two poles, because a broken conductor can whip or arc far beyond where it appears to lie. Option B is not nonsense — it is the emergency egress technique, but it is used only when staying inside is more dangerous than getting out, such as when the vehicle is on fire. Moving a conductor with a 'dry' branch and trusting examination gloves are both fatal misconceptions: nothing the crew carries is rated for distribution voltages.
questions.explanationZh: 车身正在把电流从乘员周围导走，而车辆四周的地面可能形成电压逐圈下降的跨步电压区；一脚踏出去就跨接了这个电位差，可能当场致命。所以患者留在车内，机组退到至少两根电杆之间的距离之外，因为断落的导线可能甩动或拉弧，远远超出它看上去所在的位置。B 并不是胡说——那是紧急脱离技术，但只在留在车内比出来更危险时才用，例如车辆起火。用「干燥的」树枝挑导线、以及指望检查手套绝缘，都是会致命的误解：机组随身携带的任何东西都达不到配电电压的绝缘等级。

questions.questionEn: The crew is dispatched to an 'unknown medical' at a house. On arrival there is a strong smell of natural gas at the front door and nobody answers the knock. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 机组被派往一处住宅处理「不明医疗事件」。到场时前门处有浓烈的天然气味，敲门无人应答。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Enter quickly, open the windows to ventilate, and search for the patient
options.zh: 迅速进屋，打开窗户通风，同时搜寻患者

options.en: Withdraw immediately to a safe distance without operating any switch, doorbell, radio or phone within the hazard area, and request the fire department and the gas utility
options.zh: 立即撤到安全距离，在危险区域内不操作任何开关、门铃、电台或手机，并请求消防部门和燃气公司到场

options.en: Turn on the interior lights so that the crew can see while searching
options.zh: 打开室内灯，方便机组在搜寻时看清楚

options.en: Use the portable radio inside the house to update dispatch on what has been found
options.zh: 在屋内用便携电台向调度报告发现的情况

questions.explanationEn: An atmosphere at explosive concentration needs only an ignition source, and the crew is carrying several: a doorbell, a light switch, a flashlight that is not intrinsically safe, a portable radio, a phone. Every one of those produces a spark at its contacts. There is no version of this call in which a paramedic enters to search — the fire department has meters and protective equipment and the crew does not. Ventilating by opening windows from inside a flammable atmosphere is a firefighting task, not a first-aid one, and options C and D name the specific ignition sources that have killed responders.
questions.explanationZh: 达到爆炸浓度的气体环境只差一个点火源，而机组身上正带着好几个：门铃、灯开关、非防爆手电、便携电台、手机——它们的触点都会打火。这类任务没有任何一种版本是让救护员进屋搜寻的：消防部门有检测仪和防护装备，机组没有。在可燃气体环境里开窗通风是消防作业而不是急救作业，而 C 和 D 正是曾经害死过救援人员的那两个具体点火源。

questions.questionEn: Which description best represents correct body mechanics when lifting the end of a loaded stretcher from ground level?
questions.questionZh: 从地面高度抬起载着患者的担架一端时，下列哪项描述最符合正确的人体力学？

options.en: Bend at the waist with the legs straight and lift using the back muscles
options.zh: 双腿伸直、从腰部弯下去，用背部肌肉发力抬起

options.en: Hold the load at arm's length, so that the abdomen and groin are protected
options.zh: 把重物端在手臂伸直的距离上，以保护腹部和腹股沟

options.en: Begin the lift and then twist the torso, so that the load is already moving toward the ambulance
options.zh: 一开始抬就同时扭转躯干，让重物顺势朝救护车方向移动

options.en: Keep the back straight and locked, bend at the knees and hips, hold the load close to the body, and straighten the legs to raise it
options.zh: 保持背部平直并锁定，屈膝屈髋，把重物贴近身体，靠伸直双腿把它抬起来

questions.explanationEn: The back is a hinge, not a lever, and it is not built to be one. In a correct lift the spine stays in its neutral curve and locked, the hips and knees do the bending, the load is kept as close as possible to the body's centre of gravity, and the powerful thigh and gluteal muscles produce the movement. Option A is the classic injury mechanism, option B multiplies the load on the lumbar discs, and option C adds rotation under load — the worst possible combination for an intervertebral disc.
questions.explanationZh: 腰背是一个铰链，不是杠杆，也不是按杠杆设计的。正确的抬举中，脊柱保持自然生理曲度并锁定，弯曲发生在髋和膝，重物尽量贴近身体重心，动作由强大的大腿和臀肌完成。A 是最经典的受伤机制；B 成倍放大了腰椎间盘的负荷；C 在负重状态下加入旋转，对椎间盘来说是最糟糕的组合。

questions.questionEn: Why must a load be kept as close to the body as possible during a lift?
questions.questionZh: 抬举时为什么必须把重物尽量贴近身体？

options.en: Because the further the load is from the spine, the longer the lever arm and the greater the compressive force on the lumbar discs
options.zh: 因为重物离脊柱越远，力臂越长，腰椎间盘承受的压力就越大

options.en: Because holding the load close keeps the patient warmer during the transfer
options.zh: 因为贴近身体可以在转移过程中让患者更暖和

options.en: Because it allows the lift to be completed by fewer people
options.zh: 因为这样可以用更少的人完成抬举

options.en: Because it makes the crew appear more professional to bystanders and family
options.zh: 因为这样在旁观者和家属眼里显得更专业

questions.explanationEn: This is simple mechanics: the load on the lower back is roughly the weight multiplied by its horizontal distance from the spine, so a 20 kg object held 50 cm out loads the lumbar spine several times more heavily than the same object held against the abdomen. It is the reason you step in close before lifting instead of reaching, and the reason you lower a bed rail rather than lift across it.
questions.explanationZh: 这是简单的力学：腰背承受的负荷约等于重量乘以它到脊柱的水平距离，所以同样 20 公斤的东西，端在离身体 50 厘米处对腰椎的压力是贴在腹前时的数倍。这正是为什么要先走近再抬、而不是伸长手去够，也是为什么要先放下床栏、而不是隔着床栏抬人。

questions.questionEn: A paramedic is about to lift the foot end of a loaded stretcher from ground level. How should the feet and hands be positioned?
questions.questionZh: 救护员准备从地面高度抬起载人担架的足端。双脚和双手应该怎么放？

options.en: Feet together and arms crossed in front of the body, to keep the load centred
options.zh: 双脚并拢、双臂在身前交叉，以保持负荷居中

options.en: Up on the toes, to gain the height needed to clear the stretcher wheels
options.zh: 踮起脚尖，以获得抬过担架轮所需的高度

options.en: Feet flat and about shoulder-width apart with the weight through the heels and arches, and hands at least shoulder-width apart in a palms-up power grip
options.zh: 双脚踏平、约与肩同宽，重量落在足跟和足弓上；双手至少与肩同宽，掌心向上做「有力抓握」

options.en: One foot placed up on the stretcher frame for leverage, with both hands together in the middle of the bar
options.zh: 一只脚踩在担架车架上借力，双手并拢握在横杆中间

questions.explanationEn: A wide, flat base of support with the weight through the heels keeps the lift stable and lets the leg muscles drive it, while a power grip with the palms up and the hands well apart spreads the load across the whole hand and stops the bar rolling. Feet together and hands together both destabilize the load at the exact moment it leaves the ground, and rising onto the toes puts the entire lift on top of the smallest possible base of support.
questions.explanationZh: 宽而平稳的支撑面加上重量落在足跟，能让抬举保持稳定并由腿部肌肉驱动；掌心向上、双手拉开距离的「有力抓握」把负荷分散到整个手掌，也能防止横杆在手里转动。双脚并拢和双手并拢都会让重物在刚离地的那一刻失稳，而踮脚尖等于把整个抬举放在最小的支撑面上。

questions.questionEn: Having lifted the head end of a loaded stretcher, a paramedic needs to turn it 90 degrees to line it up with the ambulance doors. What is the correct technique?
questions.questionZh: 救护员抬起载人担架的头端后，需要把它转 90 度才能对准救护车后门。正确的做法是什么？

options.en: Twisting under load is acceptable as long as the knees stay bent
options.zh: 只要膝盖保持弯曲，负重状态下扭腰是可以接受的

options.en: Move the feet and pivot the whole body as a unit, so that the shoulders and hips turn together rather than twisting the loaded spine
options.zh: 移动双脚、整个身体作为一个整体转向，让肩和髋同步转动，而不是扭转负重的脊柱

options.en: Twisting under load is acceptable as long as the load is light
options.zh: 只要重量不大，负重状态下扭腰是可以接受的

options.en: Twist toward the dominant side only, since that side is stronger
options.zh: 只朝惯用手一侧扭转，因为那一侧力量更强

questions.explanationEn: Rotation combined with compression is the mechanism that tears intervertebral discs, and it does not become safe because the knees are bent, because the load is light, or because the turn is toward your strong side. Turning is done with the feet: take small steps so the hips and shoulders stay in the same plane and the spine simply travels with the body. It is also why the crew agrees on the direction of travel before the lift, rather than discovering mid-carry that a turn is needed.
questions.explanationZh: 旋转叠加压缩正是撕裂椎间盘的机制，它不会因为膝盖弯着、重量较轻或朝着「有力的一侧」而变安全。转向要靠脚：迈小步，让髋和肩保持在同一平面上，脊柱只是随身体整体移动。这也是为什么机组要在抬起之前就商量好行进方向，而不是抬到一半才发现必须转弯。

questions.questionEn: A conscious, cooperative patient with abdominal pain must be brought down from a second-floor apartment. The staircase is narrow and turns at a landing. There is no suspicion of spinal injury and the vital signs are normal. Which device is most appropriate?
questions.questionZh: 一名清醒、配合的腹痛患者需要从二楼公寓搬到楼下。楼梯狭窄，中间有转角平台。没有脊柱损伤的怀疑，生命体征正常。最合适的器材是什么？

options.en: A long spine board, carried head-first down the stairs
options.zh: 长脊板，头端朝前抬下楼

options.en: The wheeled stretcher, tilted and carried by the two-person crew
options.zh: 轮式担架，由两人机组倾斜着抬下去

options.en: Assisting the patient to walk down between the two paramedics
options.zh: 由两名救护员一左一右扶着患者自己走下楼

options.en: A stair chair, operated by trained crew at the head and foot with a spotter on the stairs
options.zh: 楼梯椅，由受过训练的机组一头一尾操作，另加一名在楼梯上的护持人员

questions.explanationEn: A stair chair is purpose-built for a seated, cooperative patient on a staircase that a stretcher cannot negotiate: it is compact, allows a controlled descent, and keeps the patient's weight low and close to the operators. The wheeled stretcher will not make a turning staircase, and a long spine board is an extrication device that would put a supine patient at a steep angle for no reason. Walking a patient with undifferentiated abdominal pain down stairs risks a syncopal episode on the steepest part of the route, which is exactly where you cannot catch them.
questions.explanationZh: 楼梯椅正是为「清醒、能坐，而担架下不去的楼梯」这一情形设计的：体积小、可控速下降，还能让患者的重量保持低位并贴近操作者。轮式担架过不了转角楼梯；长脊板是脱困器材，会毫无必要地把仰卧的患者立成陡角。让一名原因未明的腹痛患者自己走楼梯，则可能在整条路线最陡的地方发生晕厥，而那恰恰是你接不住他的地方。

questions.questionEn: A patient on the second floor has a blood pressure of 78/50, is pale and diaphoretic, and is drifting in and out of alertness. The stairwell is narrow. The partner suggests using the stair chair because it is the quickest way down. What is the most appropriate decision?
questions.questionZh: 一名患者在二楼，血压 78/50，面色苍白、大汗，意识时清时糊。楼梯狭窄。搭档建议用楼梯椅，因为这是下楼最快的方式。最恰当的决定是什么？

options.en: Do not use the stair chair; move the patient supine on a device such as a flexible stretcher or a scoop, with enough personnel to control the descent
options.zh: 不用楼梯椅；改用软担架或铲式担架等器材让患者保持仰卧，并调足人手控制下降过程

options.en: Use the stair chair, because speed of transport is the priority in a hypotensive patient
options.zh: 使用楼梯椅，因为低血压患者的首要任务是尽快转运

options.en: Walk the patient down with a paramedic supporting each arm
options.zh: 由两名救护员一左一右扶着患者走下楼

options.en: Carry the patient down over one paramedic's shoulders, since the stairwell is narrow
options.zh: 由一名救护员把患者扛在肩上下楼，因为楼梯很窄

questions.explanationEn: A stair chair sits the patient upright, and sitting a hypotensive patient up removes the venous return that is currently keeping the brain perfused; patients have arrested on the stairs for exactly this reason. This is the case where the fastest way down is the wrong way down — get more hands, keep the patient flat on a flexible stretcher or a scoop, and accept the extra few minutes. Walking is worse still, and a shoulder carry is unsafe for both the patient and the carrier on a staircase.
questions.explanationZh: 楼梯椅要求患者坐直，而把低血压患者扶坐起来，等于取消了此刻仍在维持脑灌注的静脉回流；确实有患者正是因此在楼梯上发生心跳骤停。这是「下楼最快的方式恰恰是错的」的典型情形：叫更多人手，用软担架或铲式担架让患者保持平卧，接受多花的那几分钟。让患者自己走更糟，而在楼梯上肩扛对患者和搬运者都不安全。

questions.questionEn: An 82-year-old woman has fallen in a small bathroom and has a shortened, externally rotated leg suggesting a hip fracture. She is lying on the floor between the toilet and the bathtub. Which device best allows the crew to move her with the least movement of the injured limb?
questions.questionZh: 一名 82 岁女性在狭小的卫生间摔倒，患肢短缩、外旋，提示髋部骨折。她躺在马桶和浴缸之间的地面上。哪种器材能让机组在最少移动患肢的情况下把她搬走？

options.en: A long spine board, applied after a full log roll onto the board
options.zh: 长脊板，先完整轴向翻身把她滚到板上

options.en: A stair chair, since she has to be brought out through the doorway
options.zh: 楼梯椅，因为她必须被搬出门

options.en: A scoop stretcher, separated into halves, worked in from each side and reconnected underneath her
options.zh: 铲式担架，拆成两半从两侧分别插入，再在她身下扣合

options.en: A flexible (soft) stretcher, slid under her after rolling her onto the injured side
options.zh: 软担架，先把她翻向受伤的一侧，再把担架塞到身下

questions.explanationEn: The scoop splits lengthwise so that each half can be worked in from either side and locked together beneath the patient — she is lifted essentially where she lies, which is the entire point when the injury is a painful hip fracture in a space too small to log roll. A long board requires a full roll, and option D specifies rolling her onto the fractured hip, which is both agonizing and avoidable. A stair chair requires her to sit, which a fractured hip will not tolerate.
questions.explanationZh: 铲式担架可以纵向分开，两半从左右两侧分别插入并在患者身下锁合——她基本上是在原地被抬起来的，这正是在小到无法轴向翻身的空间里搬运疼痛的髋部骨折患者所需要的。长脊板需要完整翻身；D 更是明确要求把她翻向骨折的那一侧，既剧痛又完全可以避免。楼梯椅要求她坐起来，髋部骨折的患者无法忍受。

questions.questionEn: A trauma patient has been extricated from a vehicle on a long spine board and is now beside the ambulance stretcher. What should be done with the board?
questions.questionZh: 一名创伤患者已被用长脊板从车内脱困，现在已到救护车担架旁。接下来该如何处理这块脊板？

options.en: Leave the patient strapped to the board for the entire transport, since it provides the best immobilization
options.zh: 让患者整趟转运都固定在脊板上，因为它提供最好的固定效果

options.en: Transfer the patient off the board onto the padded stretcher while maintaining spinal precautions, because the board is an extrication and transfer device rather than a transport surface
options.zh: 在维持脊柱保护的前提下把患者从脊板转移到有软垫的担架上，因为脊板是脱困和转移器材，不是转运用的躺卧面

options.en: Leave the patient on the board but remove the straps, so that the patient is more comfortable
options.zh: 让患者留在脊板上，但把约束带解开，好让患者舒服一些

options.en: Leave the patient on the board and place the board directly onto the hospital bed at the receiving facility
options.zh: 让患者留在脊板上，到院后连板一起放到医院病床上

questions.explanationEn: A rigid board causes measurable pressure injury within tens of minutes, is painful enough to confuse the later abdominal and back examination, and restricts chest wall movement in a patient who may already be compromised. Current practice uses it to get the patient out and across, and then removes it while keeping the spine in line, with the patient secured to a padded stretcher. Option C is the worst of both worlds: all the discomfort of the board with none of the securing.
questions.explanationZh: 硬质脊板在几十分钟内就会造成可测量的压力性损伤，其疼痛程度足以干扰之后的腹部和背部查体，还会限制本就可能受损的胸廓活动。现行做法是用它把患者「取出来、转过去」，随后在保持脊柱轴线的前提下撤走，把患者固定在有软垫的担架上。C 是两头都不讨好：脊板的所有不适都留着，固定作用却没有了。

questions.questionEn: A patient must be moved out of a mobile home through a hallway that is too narrow for the wheeled stretcher and has a 90-degree turn that a stair chair cannot negotiate. What is the most appropriate solution?
questions.questionZh: 一名患者需要从活动房屋中搬出，但走廊太窄，轮式担架进不去，而且有一个连楼梯椅也转不过来的 90 度直角。最合适的解决办法是什么？

options.en: Drag the patient out to the door by the wrists, then load onto the stretcher
options.zh: 抓住手腕把患者拖到门口，再抬上担架

options.en: Ask the patient to crawl to the door unaided
options.zh: 请患者自己爬到门口

options.en: Remove the door frame so that the wheeled stretcher can pass
options.zh: 拆掉门框，让轮式担架能通过

options.en: Use a flexible (soft) stretcher with handles along both sides, with enough personnel to carry it level through the turn
options.zh: 使用两侧带把手的软担架，调足人手保持水平抬着通过转角

questions.explanationEn: A flexible stretcher is designed for exactly this: it conforms to the space, its handles are distributed along its length so several people can share the load, and it can be angled through a turn that a rigid device cannot make. What it needs is bodies rather than force, so the correct instinct is to call for extra hands. Dragging by the wrists is an emergency move reserved for immediate danger, asking a patient to crawl abandons care, and dismantling the building is not the crew's job when a purpose-built device is on the ambulance.
questions.explanationZh: 软担架正是为这种情形设计的：它能顺应空间形状，沿长度分布的把手让多人分担重量，还能在硬质器材过不去的转角处倾斜通过。它需要的是人手而不是蛮力，所以正确的直觉是叫增援。抓手腕拖拽只用于有即刻危险的紧急搬移；让患者自己爬等于放弃照护；而车上明明有专用器材时，拆房子并不是机组该干的事。

questions.questionEn: A patient must be brought down from the eighth floor of an apartment building. The building's only elevator is too small to take the wheeled stretcher at full length. What is the most appropriate approach?
questions.questionZh: 一名患者需要从公寓八楼搬下来。楼里唯一的电梯装不下完全展开的轮式担架。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Determine whether the patient can be brought into the elevator by another means — on a stair chair, or on the stretcher with the back raised and the foot end lowered — and use the elevator; take the stairs only if the elevator genuinely cannot be used
options.zh: 先设法看能否换个方式进电梯——改用楼梯椅，或把担架背板升起、足端放低——然后走电梯；只有在电梯确实用不了时才走楼梯

options.en: Carry the patient down eight flights on a stair chair, since the elevator has already been ruled out
options.zh: 用楼梯椅把患者抬下八层楼梯，因为电梯已经被排除

options.en: Wait for a larger service elevator to become available, regardless of how long that takes
options.zh: 一直等到有更大的货梯可用，不管要等多久

options.en: Request the fire department to bring the patient down from the balcony by ladder
options.zh: 请消防部门从阳台用云梯把患者接下来

questions.explanationEn: Eight flights of stairs is a long, high-risk carry — it is where crews get injured and where patients get dropped — so an elevator that can be made to work is almost always the right answer. Most stretchers will fit an apartment elevator once the back is raised, and if not, the patient can ride the elevator on a stair chair. Ruling the elevator out after a single glance is the error. Option C spends the patient's time to avoid thinking, and option D calls for a technical rescue in a situation that is not one.
questions.explanationZh: 八层楼梯是一段漫长而高风险的搬运——机组受伤、患者摔落大多发生在这种路线上——所以只要电梯能想办法用上，几乎总是正确答案。把担架背板升起后，大多数公寓电梯都装得下；实在不行，也可以让患者只在乘电梯这一段改坐楼梯椅。看一眼就把电梯排除掉才是错误。C 用患者的时间来换「不用动脑子」；D 则是把一个本不需要技术救援的情形当成了技术救援。

questions.questionEn: A 200 kg patient has slid to the bedroom floor and cannot get up. The two-person crew is alone, the patient is alert and uninjured, and the bedroom is cluttered. What should the crew do?
questions.questionZh: 一名 200 公斤的患者滑落到卧室地面上，无法自行起身。现场只有两人机组，患者清醒、没有受伤，卧室里堆满杂物。机组应该怎么做？

options.en: Perform the lift as a two-person crew, using correct body mechanics throughout
options.zh: 由两人机组完成抬举，全程使用正确的人体力学

options.en: Drag the patient to the hallway on a blanket, where there is more room to lift
options.zh: 先用毯子把患者拖到走廊，那里空间更大再抬

options.en: Request additional personnel and bariatric-capable lifting and transport equipment before attempting to move the patient
options.zh: 在尝试搬动之前，请求增派人手和适用于肥胖患者的搬运与转运器材

options.en: Ask the two adult family members who are present to help the crew lift
options.zh: 请现场两名成年家属帮忙一起抬

questions.explanationEn: Correct body mechanics do not change the arithmetic: two people cannot safely raise 200 kg, and attempting it is how crews end their careers and how patients get dropped. The correct answer is to stop, clear the space, and get the right number of people and the right equipment, which most services can dispatch specifically for this. Option D is the mistake crews genuinely make — untrained family members do not know how to lift, are not covered if they are injured, and are frequently older or unwell themselves.
questions.explanationZh: 正确的人体力学改变不了算术：两个人无法安全抬起 200 公斤，硬来正是机组职业生涯终结、患者被摔落的原因。正确答案是先停下来，清出空间，把足够的人手和合适的器材调来——多数机构都可以专门为此派遣资源。D 是机组真会犯的错：没受过训练的家属不知道怎么抬，受伤了也不在任何保障范围内，而且往往自己年纪也大或身体也不好。

questions.questionEn: An elderly patient has slipped off her bed and is wedged on the floor between the bed and the wall. She is alert, there is no suspicion of spinal injury, and she cannot free herself. What is the most appropriate way to move her?
questions.questionZh: 一名年长女性患者从床上滑落，卡在床和墙之间的地面上。她神志清楚，没有脊柱损伤的怀疑，自己出不来。最恰当的搬动方式是什么？

options.en: Pull her out by both arms from the head end
options.zh: 从头端抓住她的双臂把她拉出来

options.en: Move the bed away from the wall first to create working space, then move her with a flexible stretcher or a draw-sheet slide with enough personnel
options.zh: 先把床挪离墙面腾出操作空间，然后用软担架或床单平移，并配备足够人手

options.en: Lift her by grasping her clothing at the shoulders and hips
options.zh: 抓住她肩部和髋部的衣物把她提起来

options.en: Have her roll underneath the bed and come out on the far side
options.zh: 让她从床底下滚过去，从另一侧出来

questions.explanationEn: The first move in a confined-space extrication is almost always to make the space bigger, and a bed is the easiest thing in the room to move. Once the crew can work from both sides, a flexible stretcher or a draw-sheet slide moves the patient with the load shared and the spine supported. Pulling on the arms of an elderly patient risks dislocation and skin tears in fragile tissue, and lifting by clothing tears the clothing while concentrating the whole force onto a narrow band of skin.
questions.explanationZh: 狭窄空间搬运的第一步，几乎永远是把空间变大，而床是房间里最容易挪动的东西。等机组能从两侧同时操作后，用软担架或床单平移就能分担重量并托住脊柱。拉扯年长患者的手臂有脱位和撕裂脆弱皮肤的风险；抓衣物提举则会扯破衣服，还把全部力量集中在一条很窄的皮肤上。

questions.questionEn: A single crew arrives at a single-vehicle collision. The patient is unresponsive in the driver's seat and flames are visible under the engine compartment. Additional resources are two minutes away. What is the most appropriate action?
questions.questionZh: 一组机组独自到达一起单车事故现场。患者在驾驶座上失去反应，发动机舱下方已可见明火，增援还有两分钟到达。最恰当的做法是什么？

options.en: Wait for additional resources, since moving the patient without spinal precautions may cause harm
options.zh: 等待增援到达，因为不做脊柱保护就搬动患者可能造成伤害

options.en: Apply a cervical collar and a short spine board before removing the patient
options.zh: 先上颈托和短脊板，再把患者移出车外

options.en: Drag the patient sideways out of the vehicle by one arm, which is the fastest one-person technique
options.zh: 抓住一只手臂把患者从侧面拖出来，这是单人最快的方法

options.en: Perform a rapid extrication using a clothes or shoulder drag along the long axis of the body, supporting the head and neck as far as circumstances allow, and move the patient well clear of the vehicle
options.zh: 实施快速脱困：沿身体长轴用衣物拖拽或肩部拖拽，在条件允许的范围内尽量托住头颈，把患者拖到远离车辆的安全处

questions.explanationEn: This is the exception that proves the rule. Everywhere else in this topic the safest option beats the fastest one, but an immediate life threat to both patient and rescuer — fire, an unstable structure, rising water, a hostile environment — outranks the risk of spinal injury, and the patient is moved now. The technique still matters: drag along the long axis of the body so the spine moves as a unit, support the head as far as one person can, and never drag sideways or by a single limb, which levers the spine and can dislocate a shoulder. Options A and B apply the right principle at the wrong moment, which is the classic trap.
questions.explanationZh: 这是「例外恰恰印证规则」的一题。这个主题里其他所有情形都是「最安全压倒最快」，但当患者和救援者同时面临即刻的生命威胁时——起火、结构不稳、水位上涨、环境敌对——这种威胁的优先级高于脊柱损伤的风险，必须立刻搬移。不过手法仍然重要：沿身体长轴拖拽，让脊柱作为一个整体移动；单人能托住多少头颈就托多少；绝不能从侧面拖或只抓一只肢体，那会对脊柱形成杠杆作用，还可能造成肩关节脱位。A 和 B 是在错误的时机套用了正确的原则，这正是经典陷阱。

questions.questionEn: What should the crew do in the moment immediately before lifting a loaded stretcher?
questions.questionZh: 抬起载人担架之前的那一刻，机组应该做什么？

options.en: Agree who will direct the lift, confirm that everyone has a secure grip and is ready, and lift on a clearly stated command such as 'ready, lift on three — one, two, three'
options.zh: 商定由谁发令，确认每个人都抓稳、都准备好，然后按明确的口令抬起，例如「准备，数到三抬——一、二、三」

options.en: Begin the lift whenever each crew member individually feels ready, so that nobody is rushed
options.zh: 每个人各自觉得准备好了就开始抬，这样谁都不会被催促

options.en: Have the physically stronger paramedic take the heavier end without discussion, to save time
options.zh: 由体力更强的救护员直接去抬较重的一端，不必商量，以节省时间

options.en: Lift in silence, so that the patient is not alarmed by hearing the crew talk about weight
options.zh: 全程不说话地抬，以免患者听到机组讨论重量而不安

questions.explanationEn: An uncoordinated lift is an unequal lift: if one person goes early, the other takes the entire load at the worst possible angle, and that is a common mechanism both of back injury and of dropping a stretcher. One person directs, everyone confirms readiness and grip, and the count is unambiguous — 'lift on three' means the lift happens on 'three', not after it. The same applies to lowering the stretcher and to every change of direction during a carry. Talking the plan through in front of the patient is reassuring; what alarms patients is a crew that is visibly struggling.
questions.explanationZh: 没有协调的抬举就是受力不均的抬举：只要有一个人先动，另一个人就要在最糟糕的角度上独自承担全部重量，这是腰背受伤和担架脱手的常见机制。做法是一人发令、所有人确认准备与握持，而且口令必须没有歧义——「数到三抬」意味着在「三」这一下抬起，而不是数完之后。下放担架以及搬运途中每一次改变方向，都同样适用。当着患者的面把计划说清楚是让人安心的；真正让患者害怕的，是看见机组吃力挣扎。
